sources.entry: Expressa - Content Management System for powering database driven websites using JSON schemas. Provides permission management and automatic REST APIs. MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Expressa is a data-driven API middleware for Node.js/Express that creates REST endpoints and a Django-style admin UI from JSON schema collections.
summary.what_it_does: Expressa lets you define collections as JSON schemas instead of writing custom code, and it generates REST endpoints for each collection (list, get by id, query, paginate, create, replace, update, delete). An admin interface lets you create and edit collection schemas and manage role-based permissions. Collection data can be stored in MongoDB, PostgreSQL, or JSON files, with JSON-file and in-memory storage working without extra drivers. It is distributed as middleware you mount in an existing Express app rather than a full framework. Event listeners can stop or modify requests and responses, and custom Express middleware or endpoints can be added alongside it.
use_cases: Build a REST backend for a database-driven website
Define data collections with JSON schema instead of custom code
Manage CRUD permissions for user roles
Generate forms from collection schemas in a frontend
Add a basic admin interface to an Express API
Store API data as version-controllable JSON files
how_to_run: Create app.js with: var expressa = require('expressa'); app.use('/admin', expressa.admin({ apiurl: '/api/' })); app.use('/api', expressa.api());
Run: node --use-strict app.js, then open the browser at the admin path
notable: Admin UI for creating collections and editing JSON schemas, with permission management
Automatic REST endpoints generated per collection, including Mongo-style queries, pagination, and sorting
Pluggable storage: JSON files, in-memory, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL
Used as plain middleware, so it can be mixed into an existing Express app
Ecosystem packages for extending collections, Swagger docs, browser client, and CLI
caveats: README says it is not primarily meant for simple blogs or mostly static content sites
MongoDB and PostgreSQL require installing their drivers separately
Only standard JSON data types are supported; dates must be stored as ISO 8601 strings
Roadmap lists GraphQL, JWT token expiration, cookie authentication, and file uploads as not yet supported
